Apple___Apple_scab.symptoms: Olive-green to black velvety spots on leaves and fruit; leaves may pucker, curl, and drop early. Fruit develops dark, scabby lesions.
Apple___Apple_scab.causes: Fungus Venturia inaequalis, spread by wind and rain-splashed spores during cool, wet spring weather.
Apple___Apple_scab.prevention: Plant resistant cultivars, rake and destroy fallen leaves in autumn, prune for good airflow, avoid overhead irrigation.
Apple___Apple_scab.treatment: Apply protectant fungicides (e.g. captan, myclobutanil) starting at green tip and continuing through wet spring weather per label intervals.

Apple___Black_rot.symptoms: Purple-bordered leaf spots ('frog-eye leaf spot'), rotting fruit with concentric rings, and cankers on limbs.
Apple___Black_rot.causes: Fungus Botryosphaeria obtusa, overwinters in dead wood and mummified fruit.
Apple___Black_rot.prevention: Remove mummified fruit and dead wood, prune out cankers, maintain tree vigor.
Apple___Black_rot.treatment: Fungicide sprays (captan or thiophanate-methyl) timed with apple scab sprays; sanitation is equally important.

Apple___Cedar_apple_rust.symptoms: Bright orange-yellow spots on upper leaf surface, small black dots within spots, orange tube-like structures on undersides.
Apple___Cedar_apple_rust.causes: Fungus Gymnosporangium juniperi-virginianae, which needs both apple and juniper/cedar hosts to complete its lifecycle.
Apple___Cedar_apple_rust.prevention: Remove nearby juniper/cedar hosts where feasible, choose resistant apple varieties.
Apple___Cedar_apple_rust.treatment: Fungicides (myclobutanil, mancozeb) applied from pink bud stage through several weeks after petal fall.

Apple___healthy.symptoms: No visible lesions, discoloration, or deformities on the leaf.
Apple___healthy.prevention: Continue good orchard sanitation, balanced fertilization, and regular monitoring.

Corn_(maize)___Common_rust_.symptoms: Small, round to elongate, cinnamon-brown pustules scattered on both leaf surfaces.
Corn_(maize)___Common_rust_.causes: Fungus Puccinia sorghi, favored by cool, humid weather and spread by windborne spores.
Corn_(maize)___Common_rust_.prevention: Plant resistant hybrids, avoid excessive nitrogen, monitor early in the season.
Corn_(maize)___Common_rust_.treatment: Foliar fungicides (strobilurins or triazoles) if disease pressure is high and hybrid is susceptible.

Corn_(maize)___Northern_Leaf_Blight.symptoms: Long, elliptical, gray-green to tan lesions running parallel to the leaf veins.
Corn_(maize)___Northern_Leaf_Blight.causes: Fungus Exserohilum turcicum, survives in crop residue and spreads via wind and rain splash.
Corn_(maize)___Northern_Leaf_Blight.prevention: Crop rotation, resistant hybrids, tillage to bury residue.
Corn_(maize)___Northern_Leaf_Blight.treatment: Fungicide application (e.g. pyraclostrobin) if detected early and conditions favor spread.

Corn_(maize)___healthy.symptoms: Uniform green color, no lesions or pustules.
Corn_(maize)___healthy.prevention: Maintain crop rotation and monitor for early symptoms.

Grape___Black_rot.symptoms: Small brown circular leaf spots with dark borders, fruit shrivels into hard black 'mummies'.
Grape___Black_rot.causes: Fungus Guignardia bidwellii, overwinters in mummified berries and infected canes.
Grape___Black_rot.prevention: Remove mummies and infected canes during dormant pruning, improve canopy airflow.
Grape___Black_rot.treatment: Fungicide program (mancozeb, myclobutanil) from early shoot growth through berry set.

Grape___healthy.symptoms: No spotting, no shriveled fruit, normal leaf color.
Grape___healthy.prevention: Continue routine canopy management and monitoring.

Potato___Early_blight.symptoms: Dark brown spots with concentric rings ('target spot' pattern), usually starting on older, lower leaves.
Potato___Early_blight.causes: Fungus Alternaria solani, favored by warm temperatures and alternating wet/dry periods.
Potato___Early_blight.prevention: Crop rotation, balanced fertility (avoid nitrogen deficiency), remove volunteer plants and debris.
Potato___Early_blight.treatment: Fungicides such as chlorothalonil or azoxystrobin applied at first sign of symptoms.

Potato___Late_blight.symptoms: Water-soaked, pale-to-dark green lesions that rapidly turn brown/black, often with white fungal growth on leaf undersides in humid conditions.
Potato___Late_blight.causes: Oomycete Phytophthora infestans, spreads explosively in cool, wet weather (the pathogen behind the Irish potato famine).
Potato___Late_blight.prevention: Plant certified disease-free seed potatoes, destroy volunteer plants, avoid overhead irrigation.
Potato___Late_blight.treatment: Prompt fungicide application (chlorothalonil, mancozeb, or systemic oomycete-specific products); remove infected plants quickly to limit spread.

Potato___healthy.symptoms: No lesions, uniform leaf color and structure.
Potato___healthy.prevention: Continue monitoring, especially during humid weather.

Tomato___Bacterial_spot.symptoms: Small, water-soaked, greasy-looking spots on leaves and fruit that turn brown/black with yellow halos.
Tomato___Bacterial_spot.causes: Xanthomonas bacteria, spread by splashing water, contaminated tools, and infected seed.
Tomato___Bacterial_spot.prevention: Use certified disease-free seed/transplants, avoid overhead watering, rotate crops, sanitize tools.
Tomato___Bacterial_spot.treatment: Copper-based bactericides can slow spread but won't cure infected plants; remove heavily infected material.

Tomato___Early_blight.symptoms: Concentric-ring 'target spot' lesions on older leaves first, often with yellowing around the spot.
Tomato___Early_blight.causes: Fungus Alternaria solani, favored by warm, humid conditions and plant stress.
Tomato___Early_blight.prevention: Mulch to reduce soil splash, stake plants for airflow, rotate crops, avoid overhead watering.
Tomato___Early_blight.treatment: Fungicides (chlorothalonil, copper, or azoxystrobin) applied preventatively or at first symptoms.

Tomato___Late_blight.symptoms: Large, irregular, water-soaked greenish-black blotches on leaves; white mold may appear on undersides in humid conditions; fruit develops firm brown lesions.
Tomato___Late_blight.causes: Oomycete Phytophthora infestans, spreads rapidly in cool, wet weather.
Tomato___Late_blight.prevention: Avoid overhead irrigation, ensure good airflow, remove volunteer plants, use resistant varieties where available.
Tomato___Late_blight.treatment: Fast-acting fungicide application at first sign; remove and destroy infected plants promptly to prevent regional spread.

Tomato___Leaf_Mold.symptoms: Pale green/yellow spots on upper leaf surface with olive-green to grayish-purple fuzzy mold on the underside.
Tomato___Leaf_Mold.causes: Fungus Passalora fulva (syn. Fulvia fulva), thrives in high humidity, common in greenhouses.
Tomato___Leaf_Mold.prevention: Improve ventilation, reduce humidity, avoid overhead watering, space plants adequately.
Tomato___Leaf_Mold.treatment: Fungicides labeled for leaf mold; prioritize humidity/airflow control since it's a humidity-driven disease.

Tomato___Septoria_leaf_spot.symptoms: Small circular spots with dark borders and gray/tan centers, tiny black fungal fruiting bodies visible in spot centers, usually starting on lower leaves.
Tomato___Septoria_leaf_spot.causes: Fungus Septoria lycopersici, spread by splashing water and survives in plant debris.
Tomato___Septoria_leaf_spot.prevention: Mulch, avoid overhead watering, remove lower infected leaves, rotate crops.
Tomato___Septoria_leaf_spot.treatment: Fungicides (chlorothalonil or copper-based) applied at first sign and repeated per label.

Tomato___Spider_mites Two-spotted_spider.symptoms: Fine yellow stippling/speckling on leaves, fine webbing on undersides in heavy infestations, leaves may bronze and dry out.
Tomato___Spider_mites Two-spotted_spider.causes: Tetranychus urticae mite infestation, thrives in hot, dry conditions and often flares after broad-spectrum insecticide use.
Tomato___Spider_mites Two-spotted_spider.prevention: Avoid drought stress, preserve natural predators, avoid unnecessary broad-spectrum insecticide sprays.
Tomato___Spider_mites Two-spotted_spider.treatment: Insecticidal soap or horticultural oil; miticides for severe infestations; increase humidity where practical.

Tomato___Target_Spot.symptoms: Brown lesions with concentric rings similar to early blight, can appear on leaves, stems, and fruit.
Tomato___Target_Spot.causes: Fungus Corynespora cassiicola, favored by warm, humid, wet conditions.
Tomato___Target_Spot.prevention: Improve airflow, avoid leaf wetness, rotate crops, remove infected debris.
Tomato___Target_Spot.treatment: Fungicides such as chlorothalonil or azoxystrobin, applied preventatively in high-risk conditions.

Tomato___Tomato_Yellow_Leaf_Curl_Virus.symptoms: Upward curling and yellowing of leaflet margins, stunted growth, reduced fruit set.
Tomato___Tomato_Yellow_Leaf_Curl_Virus.causes: Begomovirus transmitted by the whitefly Bemisia tabaci; no cure once infected.
Tomato___Tomato_Yellow_Leaf_Curl_Virus.prevention: Control whitefly populations, use reflective mulches, plant resistant/tolerant varieties, use insect netting on seedlings.
Tomato___Tomato_Yellow_Leaf_Curl_Virus.treatment: No chemical cure; remove and destroy infected plants to reduce virus reservoir and manage whitefly vector aggressively.

Tomato___Tomato_mosaic_virus.symptoms: Mottled light/dark green mosaic pattern on leaves, leaf distortion, stunted growth, occasional fruit discoloration.
Tomato___Tomato_mosaic_virus.causes: Tobamovirus, highly stable and spread mechanically through contaminated hands, tools, and seed.
Tomato___Tomato_mosaic_virus.prevention: Use certified virus-free seed, disinfect tools, wash hands after handling tobacco products before touching plants.
Tomato___Tomato_mosaic_virus.treatment: No chemical cure; remove and destroy infected plants; sanitize thoroughly to prevent mechanical spread.

Tomato___healthy.symptoms: Uniform green foliage, no spots, curling, or mottling.
Tomato___healthy.prevention: Continue routine monitoring, crop rotation, and balanced watering.
